mainTopic: Gentile items forbidden even for benefit, the cheese story, the source for banning idol wine, and the seal rules for vinegar and cooked wine
overview: The amud opens with a משנה listing items of גוים that a Jew may not use, some of them forbidden even for benefit (איסור הנאה). These include wine, vinegar that was once wine, Hadrianic earthenware, and hides cut at the heart. It also gives רבי עקיבא's rule about meat going into and out of an idol's house, and a rule about doing business with people going to or from an idol festival. It then brings three disputes in which רבי מאיר forbids even benefit and חכמים are more lenient. Next, רבי ישמעאל asks רבי יהושע why gentile cheese is forbidden. רבי יהושע offers two reasons, and each one is challenged. Instead of answering the second challenge, he turns the talk to how a פסוק in שיר השירים is read. The גמרא then builds a chain of sources for the ban on benefit from idol wine: wine is learned from a זבח, a זבח from a מת, a מת from the עגלה ערופה, and the עגלה ערופה from קדשים. Finally, רב אשי explains that the vinegar clause, and a parallel teaching about cooked wine, show that a Jew's vinegar or cooked wine left with a gentile needs only one seal. His explanation for cooked wine continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Gentile items that are forbidden even for benefit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with a list of gentile items that are forbidden, and even benefit from them is forbidden: wine, vinegar that started as wine, Hadrianic earthenware, and hides with a hole at the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: These items of גוים are forbidden, and the prohibition covers even getting benefit from them: wine, vinegar of גוים that was wine at first, Hadrianic earthenware, and hides with a hole cut at the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a list of gentile items that a Jew may not even benefit from, such as by selling them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of being forbidden. Some things are only forbidden to eat. Things with an איסור הנאה cannot be used for any benefit at all. Every item on this list is linked to idol worship: wine that may have been poured for an idol, or a hide from an animal whose heart was cut out for an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: a ban on getting any benefit from an item, not only on eating it
Hadrianic earthenware, clay pottery named after the Roman emperor Hadrian
hides with a hole cut opposite the heart

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'forbidden' always means only 'forbidden to eat.' Here the משנה is clear that even selling these items or getting any benefit from them is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: MISHNA: These are items of gentiles that are forbidden,
and their prohibition is a ban on benefit:
Wine, and vinegar of gentiles
that was originally wine,
and Hadrianic earthenware,
and hides with a tear opposite the heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם אֲסוּרִין, וְאִיסּוּרָן אִיסּוּר הֲנָאָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gentile wine, vinegar that was once wine, Hadrianic earthenware, and hides with a hole at the heart are forbidden even for benefit.

steps.title: Only a round cut makes the hide forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a hide is forbidden only when the cut at the heart is round. If the cut is long, the hide is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: When the cut is round, the hide is forbidden. When it is long, the hide is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל narrows the last item on the list. Not every hide with a cut at the heart is forbidden, only one with a round cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shape of the cut shows how the heart was removed. A round cut points to the heart being taken out for idol worship, so the hide is forbidden. A long cut does not point to that, so the hide is permitted.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
When its tear is round, it is forbidden;
if it is long, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the case of עורות לבובין from Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hide is forbidden only if the cut at the heart is round. If the cut is long, the hide is permitted.

steps.title: Meat going into an idol's house versus meat coming out
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says meat going into an idol's house is still permitted, but meat coming out is forbidden, because it is like זבחי מתים, offerings to the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat going into a house of עבודה זרה is permitted. Meat coming out is forbidden, because it is like offerings to the dead. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא teaches that the direction the meat is moving decides whether it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the meat enters the idol's house, it has not yet been offered, so it is still permitted. Once it comes out, we assume it was offered there, so it counts as זבחי מתים. That is a name for idol offerings, since idols are lifeless.

keyTerms.meaning: offerings to the dead, meaning offerings to idols

phrases.english: Meat that enters the house of idol worship is permitted,
and meat that comes out is forbidden,
because it is like offerings to the dead,
phrases.notes: 'The dead' here means idols, which have no life in them.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat going into an idol's house is permitted. Meat coming out is forbidden as זבחי מתים.

steps.title: Doing business with people going to an idol festival
steps.stepSummary: A Jew may not do business with people on their way to an idol festival (תרפות), but may do business with people coming back from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: With people going to an idol festival, it is forbidden to do business. With people coming back, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another 'going versus coming' rule, this time about doing business with people instead of about meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the meat rule just before it. The direction of travel matters: on the way to the festival is forbidden, on the way back is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: an idol festival or idol worship
to do business (literally, to carry and to give)

phrases.english: Those going to an idol festival:
it is forbidden to do business with them,
and those coming back are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוֹלְכִין לַתַּרְפּוּת אָסוּר לָשֵׂאת וְלָתֵת עִמָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel 'going versus coming' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing business with people going to תרפות is forbidden. With people coming back, it is permitted.

steps.title: Gentile wineskins and jugs holding Jewish wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says Jewish wine stored in gentile wineskins or jugs is forbidden even for benefit. חכמים say it is forbidden, but not for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wineskins and jugs of גוים with a Jew's wine stored in them are forbidden, and the prohibition covers even benefit. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: the prohibition does not cover benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the first dispute of the משנה begins. רבי מאיר and חכמים argue over how strict the prohibition is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the wine is forbidden, probably because it soaked up gentile wine from the vessel. They disagree about the level. רבי מאיר says even benefit is forbidden. חכמים say only drinking it is forbidden, so the wine may still be used for benefit.
steps.confusionAlert: חכמים are not saying the wine is permitted. They agree it is forbidden. They only say benefit from it is not forbidden.

phrases.english: Wineskins of gentiles and their jugs,
with a Jew's wine stored in them,
are forbidden, and their prohibition is a ban on benefit,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
Their prohibition is not a ban on benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין אִיסּוּרָן אִיסּוּר הֲנָאָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: forbidden even for benefit. חכמים: forbidden, but not for benefit.

steps.title: Leftover grape seeds and skins
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says gentile grape seeds and skins are forbidden even for benefit. חכמים say wet ones are forbidden and dry ones are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grape seeds and grape skins of גוים are forbidden, and the prohibition covers even benefit. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: wet ones are forbidden, dry ones are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second dispute. The topic is the leftovers from pressing grapes into wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר forbids all of these leftovers, even for benefit. חכמים draw a line based on moisture: wet leftovers still have wine in them and are forbidden, but dry ones have no wine left and are permitted.

phrases.english: Grape seeds and grape skins of gentiles
are forbidden, and their prohibition is a ban on benefit,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
Moist ones are forbidden; dry ones are permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: grape seeds and skins are forbidden even for benefit. חכמים: wet ones are forbidden, dry ones are permitted.

steps.title: Fish brine and cheese of בית אונייקי
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says gentile מורייס and cheese of בית אונייקי are forbidden even for benefit. חכמים say benefit from them is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: מורייס and cheese of בית אונייקי belonging to גוים are forbidden, and the prohibition covers even benefit. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: the prohibition does not cover benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last dispute in this part of the משנה, about two gentile food products.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern matches the wineskins dispute. Both sides agree these foods are forbidden. רבי מאיר says even benefit is forbidden, while חכמים say benefit is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a fish brine or fish sauce
cheese from a place called בית אונייקי

steps.whatToRemember: Throughout this משנה, רבי מאיר keeps saying 'forbidden even for benefit.' חכמים agree the items are forbidden, but they are more lenient: either benefit is allowed, or, for grape leftovers, only the wet ones are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוּרְיָיס, וּגְבִינַת בֵּית אוּנְיָיקִי שֶׁל גּוֹיִם —
phrases.english: Fish brine, and cheese of Beit Unyaki belonging to gentiles,
are forbidden, and their prohibition is a ban on benefit,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
Their prohibition is not a ban on benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוּרְיָיס, וּגְבִינַת בֵּית אוּנְיָיקִי שֶׁל גּוֹיִם אֲסוּרִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: מורייס and cheese of בית אונייקי are forbidden even for benefit. חכמים: forbidden, but not for benefit.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל asks why gentile cheese is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that while walking on the road, רבי ישמעאל asked רבי יהושע what the reason is for the ban on גבינות גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: רבי ישמעאל asked רבי יהושע, while they were walking on the road: For what reason did they forbid the cheeses of gentiles?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which רבי ישמעאל asks רבי יהושע for the reason behind the ban on gentile cheese. This question sets up a back-and-forth between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step we learned that one kind of gentile cheese, from בית אונייקי, is forbidden. Now someone asks why the חכמים forbade gentile cheese at all. The rest of this section tests each reason that is offered.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael asked Rabbi Yehoshua
while they were walking on the road,
he said to him: For what reason
did they forbid the cheeses of gentiles?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָסְרוּ גְּבִינוֹת גּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the cheese rule given in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the חכמים forbade gentile cheese.

steps.title: First answer: curdled with the stomach of a נבילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that gentiles curdle the cheese using the stomach of a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because they curdle it with the stomach of a נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives his first reason: the cheese is made to set using the stomach of an animal that was not properly slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheese is made firm by adding something from an animal's stomach. If that stomach comes from a נבילה, the idea is that the forbidden animal makes the cheese forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: They curdle it, they make it set (into cheese)
The stomach, used to curdle milk into cheese
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: He said to him: Because they curdle it
with the stomach of a נבילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּקֵיבָה שֶׁל נְבֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cheese is curdled with the stomach of a נבילה.

steps.title: Challenge: even an עולה's stomach is treated leniently
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל objects that the stomach of an עולה is more severe than that of a נבילה, yet it is treated leniently. So a נבילה's stomach should not make cheese forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But isn't the stomach of an עולה more severe than the stomach of a נבילה? And they said: A כהן who is not squeamish may swallow it raw. The others did not agree with him, but they said: One may not benefit from it, yet there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל challenges the first answer by comparing it to the stomach of an עולה, a holy offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is holy, which is more severe than a נבילה. Yet one opinion lets a כהן swallow its stomach contents, and even the other opinion says only that one should not benefit, and there is no מעילה if one does. If the stomach of something so holy is treated this leniently, the stomach of a נבילה should surely not forbid the cheese.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose mind is relaxed, meaning not squeamish about what he eats
Liable for מעילה, misuse of holy property

steps.confusionAlert: שׂוֹרְפָה here does not mean "burns it." It means "swallows it."

phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't the stomach of an עולה
more severe than the stomach of a נבילה?
They said: A כהן who is not squeamish
may swallow it raw,
and they did not agree with him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is whoever gave the lenient opinion about the כהן. The other חכמים argued with it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ: אֵין נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין!
phrases.english: but they said: One may not benefit from it, and one is not liable for מעילה!
phrases.notes: So even the stricter view treats it lightly. Using it is not the serious sin of misusing holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא קֵיבַת עוֹלָה חֲמוּרָה מִקֵּיבַת נְבֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a נבילה's stomach makes gentile cheese forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר-style comparison: the stomach of a holy עולה is treated leniently, so the stomach of a less severe נבילה should be treated leniently too.

steps.title: Second answer: curdled with stomachs of idol-worship calves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע gives a new reason: the cheese is curdled with the stomach of calves used for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because they curdle it with the stomach of calves of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע drops the נבילה reason and gives a different one: the calves were offered to idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal used for עבודה זרה is far more severely forbidden than a נבילה. That would explain why its stomach could make the cheese forbidden, and the עולה comparison would no longer work.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because they curdle it
with the stomach of calves of עבודה זרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּקֵיבַת עֶגְלֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason that step 10 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the reason with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban comes from the stomach of a נבילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban comes from the stomach of calves used for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Challenge: then why is benefit allowed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל objects: if the cheese comes from idol-worship calves, it should be forbidden even for benefit, so why didn't the חכמים forbid that?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, why didn't they forbid it for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל challenges the second answer too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything from עבודה זרה is forbidden even for benefit. But the חכמים only forbade eating the cheese (step 7), not benefiting from it. So the idol-calf reason does not fit the actual rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit, any use, such as selling

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
why didn't they forbid it for benefit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה לֹא אֲסָרוּהָ בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the cheese is forbidden because of idol-worship calves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Things from עבודה זרה are forbidden even for benefit, but this cheese is only forbidden to eat, so that reason cannot be right.

steps.title: רבי יהושע changes the subject to a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Instead of answering, רבי יהושע turns the conversation to another matter and asks רבי ישמעאל how he reads a פסוק in שיר השירים: "דֹּדֶיךָ" or "דֹּדַיִךְ".
steps.simpleTranslation: He turned him to another matter. He said to him: ישמעאל, how do you read: "For Your love is better than wine," or "For your love is better"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע does not answer the challenge. He changes the topic by asking about how a word in a פסוק is read. This sets up the next part of the conversation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings differ by one vowel. דֹּדֶיךָ is masculine ("Your love"), and דֹּדַיִךְ is feminine ("your love"). Notice that the question about the reason for the cheese ban is left without an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned him to another topic

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the פסוק question is the answer about the cheese. רבי יהושע is changing the subject on purpose, and the cheese question stays open.

phrases.english: He turned him to another matter,
he said to him: Yishmael,
how do you read
"For Your love is better than wine"
or "For your love is better"?
phrases.notes: Same words, but here "your" is read as feminine instead of masculine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of answering the challenge in step 12, רבי יהושע steers the talk to a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי ישמעאל reads the word in the פסוק as masculine (דֹּדֶיךָ) or feminine (דֹּדַיִךְ).

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל reads the verse in the feminine
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that the פסוק reads "כי טובים דודיך", spoken to a female.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to him: "For your love (said to a woman) is better than wine."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers רבי יהושע's question from step 13. He reads the word in the feminine form, as if it is spoken to a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether the word is masculine (דֹּדֶיךָ, spoken to a man) or feminine (דֹּדַיִךְ, spoken to a woman). רבי ישמעאל picks the feminine reading. This sets up רבי יהושע's next move.

keyTerms.meaning: Song of Songs, the book the פסוק comes from

phrases.english: He said to him: "For your love (feminine) is better."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 1:2. רבי ישמעאל reads it as spoken to a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reading question רבי יהושע asked in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word is read in the feminine: דודיך.

steps.title: רבי יהושע proves the verse is masculine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the feminine reading, because the very next פסוק, "לריח שמניך טובים", is clearly masculine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: It is not so, because the next פסוק teaches about it: "Your oils have a good smell" (spoken to a man).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע tells רבי ישמעאל his reading is wrong. He proves it from the next פסוק, which is spoken to a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "שמניך" in the next פסוק is masculine. Since both פסוקים are said to the same person, the first one must be masculine too. So the right reading is דודיך, spoken to a man.

keyTerms.meaning: Its neighbor (the next פסוק) teaches about it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע never answered the cheese question here. He changed the subject on purpose, and this back-and-forth about the פסוק is that change of subject, not an answer about cheese.

phrases.english: He said to him: The matter is not so,
for its neighbor teaches about it:
phrases.notes: "Its neighbor" means the very next פסוק, שיר השירים 1:3.

phrases.english: "Your oils have a good smell."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין הַדָּבָר כֵּן, שֶׁהֲרֵי חֲבֵירוֹ מְלַמֵּד עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ישמעאל's reading from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The feminine reading of the word in שיר השירים 1:2.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The next פסוק uses a masculine form, so the first פסוק must be masculine too.

steps.title: Where do we learn that idol wine is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source that wine of idol worship is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Wine, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins its discussion of the משנה. It asks where we learn that wine of idol worship is forbidden, and this question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids benefit from gentile wine (יין נסך), so the גמרא wants a פסוק behind that rule. This is a request for a source, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Wine, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we learn that wine of idol worship is forbidden for benefit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story ends and the גמרא begins a new discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that idol wine is forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: Wine is compared to an idol offering
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה learns from a פסוק that puts offerings and wine together: just as an idol offering is forbidden for benefit, so is the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה said: The פסוק says, "Who ate the fat of their offerings and drank the wine of their drink-offering." Just as an offering is forbidden for benefit, wine is also forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה gives the source. One פסוק mentions idol offerings and idol wine side by side, so they share the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two are written together, wine takes the law of a זבח, and is forbidden even for benefit. This answer only moves the question back one level, because now we need to know why a זבח is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering (here, one brought to an idol)
Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: רבה בר אבוה said,
the פסוק says:
"Who ate the fat of their offerings,
and drank the wine of their drink-offering."
Just as an offering is forbidden for benefit,
so too wine is forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wine is learned from a זבח, because the פסוק puts them together.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the offering itself is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that an idol offering is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offering itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the next question in the chain. If wine is learned from a זבח, where do we learn that a זבח is forbidden? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 17 only works if a זבח is surely forbidden for benefit. So the גמרא checks that base.

phrases.english: The offering itself, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the base that step 17 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that an idol offering is forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: An idol offering is compared to a dead body
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק calls idol offerings "offerings of the dead", so just as a dead body is forbidden for benefit, so is an idol offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "They attached themselves to בעל פעור and ate offerings of the dead." Just as a dead body is forbidden for benefit, an offering is also forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק links idol offerings to a dead body. So the offering gets the law of a מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls offerings to the idol "זבחי מתים", offerings of the dead. That connects a זבח to a מת, which is forbidden for benefit. Now the chain leans on a new link, the מת.

phrases.english: As it is written: "They attached themselves to בעל פעור,
and ate offerings of the dead."
Just as a dead body is forbidden for benefit,
so too an offering is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A זבח is learned from a מת, because the פסוק calls idol offerings "offerings of the dead".

steps.title: Where do we learn that a dead body is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a dead body is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the dead body itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the last link in the chain: where do we learn that a מת is forbidden for benefit? This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 assumed that a מת is forbidden for benefit. Now the גמרא wants a source for that too.

phrases.english: And the dead body itself, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the base that step 19 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a dead body is forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: A dead body is learned from the עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: Through a גזרה שוה on the word "שם", a dead body (Miriam's death) is compared to the עגלה ערופה, which is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from "there" and "there" from the עגלה ערופה. Here it is written: "And מרים died there," and there it is written: "And they shall break the neck of the calf there in the valley." Just as there it is forbidden for benefit, so too here it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the chain. The word "שם" (there) appears both by מרים's death and by the עגלה ערופה, so a dead body gets the same law as the calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה is treated as forbidden for benefit. The shared word "שם" makes a גזרה שוה, so a מת is also forbidden for benefit. The chain is not finished yet: the next step asks how we know the עגלה ערופה itself is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both
The calf whose neck is broken when a body is found and the killer is not known

phrases.english: It is learned from "there" and "there" from the calf whose neck is broken.
Here it is written: "And מרים died there,"
and there it is written:
"And they shall break the calf's neck there in the valley."
Just as there, it is forbidden for benefit,
so too here, it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 and completes the chain of sources.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מת is learned from the עגלה ערופה through the גזרה שוה of "שם".
steps.whyThisMatters: It links the ban on benefit from a מת to the עגלה ערופה. The next steps then show where the עגלה ערופה's own ban comes from.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the עגלה ערופה itself is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, by the עגלה ערופה, how do we know it is forbidden for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes one more step back in the chain. It now asks how we know the עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, a dead body was learned from the עגלה ערופה through a גזרה שוה. That proof only works if the עגלה ערופה is itself forbidden for benefit. So now the גמרא needs a source for that.

keyTerms.meaning: And there, meaning the case we just used as the source
From where do we know this?
The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: 'There' means the עגלה ערופה from step 21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the case that step 21 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: The word 'atonement' links the עגלה ערופה to sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the תורה uses the word 'כפרה' for the עגלה ערופה, just as it does for קדשים, which are forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: 'Atonement' is written about it, just like for sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי gives the last link in the chain. The עגלה ערופה is called a 'כפרה', just like קדשים, so it is forbidden for benefit just as קדשים are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole chain is now in place. יין נסך is learned from idol offerings, idol offerings from a dead body, a dead body from the עגלה ערופה, and the עגלה ערופה from קדשים. קדשים are clearly forbidden for benefit, so the chain rests on solid ground.
steps.whatToRemember: The full chain: יין נסך ← idol offerings ← a dead body ← עגלה ערופה ← קדשים. Each link is forbidden for benefit because of the one after it.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
'Atonement' is written about it, as with sacrifices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 and closes the chain of sources.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word כפרה used for the עגלה ערופה compares it to קדשים, which are forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: The משנה: gentile vinegar that started as wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that gentiles' vinegar which was originally wine is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the vinegar of gentiles that was originally wine is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next case, gentile vinegar that started out as wine. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts this vinegar among the forbidden items. The words 'that was originally wine' are the key point. This vinegar was once gentile wine, which was already forbidden.

phrases.english: And the vinegar of gentiles
that was originally wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַחוֹמֶץ שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שֶׁהָיָה מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gentile vinegar that began as wine is forbidden.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say this, since souring should not remove a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! Just because it soured, should its prohibition go away?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for teaching something that seems obvious. Wine that was forbidden does not become permitted just because it turned sour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the classic 'פשיטא' challenge. A משנה should not waste words on something we would know anyway. So the גמרא expects there must be some hidden lesson here.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a teaching is unnecessary)

phrases.english: It's obvious!
Because it soured, should its prohibition go away?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the משנה's ruling from step 24 needed to be taught at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that gentile vinegar from wine is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forbidden item does not become permitted just because it changes into vinegar, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב אשי: our vinegar with a gentile needs only one seal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's real lesson is that Jewish vinegar left with a gentile needs only a single seal. Gentiles don't pour vinegar as an offering, and with a seal they won't bother to forge one in order to swap it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This teaches that our vinegar in a gentile's hands does not need a seal within a seal. If you worry he poured it as an offering, they don't pour vinegar. If you worry he swapped it, since there is a seal, he won't bother forging one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains what the משנה is really teaching. Vinegar is treated more leniently than wine, so a Jew's vinegar left with a gentile is fine with just one seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a Jew's wine left with a gentile needs two seals (חותם בתוך חותם). That protects against two worries: that the gentile used it for an idol offering, and that he swapped it for his own. For vinegar, the first worry does not apply at all, and for the second worry one seal is enough of a deterrent.

keyTerms.meaning: A seal within a seal, a double seal
Being poured as an idol offering

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the gentile's own vinegar is permitted. That stays forbidden. The lesson is about a Jew's vinegar that was left in a gentile's hands.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This comes to teach us
that our vinegar in the hand of a gentile
does not need a seal within a seal.
If because of pouring it as an offering, they don't pour it,
and if because of swapping it,
since there is a seal,
he won't go to the trouble of forging it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא אֲתָא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 25 by pointing to a hidden lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Hidden lesson: the משנה teaches a related leniency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems only to repeat the obvious, that soured wine stays forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: By saying the vinegar is forbidden because it 'was originally wine', the משנה implies that vinegar as vinegar is not poured to idols. So a Jew's vinegar left with a gentile needs only one seal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical rule: vinegar left with a gentile needs one seal, not two.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: gentile cooked wine is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא reports a teaching that gentiles' cooked wine, which was originally ordinary wine, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: We learned that gentile cooked wine which was originally wine is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא brings a teaching that matches the vinegar case, this time about cooked wine. This sets up the same question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording follows the vinegar line closely, 'that was originally wine'. Here the change is cooking instead of souring. The ruling is the same: it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said: We learned:
cooked wine of gentiles
that was originally wine is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel teaching about cooked wine, modeled on the vinegar case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gentile cooked wine that started as ordinary wine is forbidden.

steps.title: Again: isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this needed saying, since cooking should not remove a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! Just because it was cooked, should its prohibition go away?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same challenge as before. Forbidden wine does not become permitted just because someone cooked it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works exactly like step 25, with 'cooked' in place of 'soured'. Again the גמרא is looking for a hidden lesson.

phrases.english: It's obvious!
Because it was cooked, should its prohibition go away?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אילעא's teaching the same way step 25 challenged the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's teaching that gentile cooked wine is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cooking does not undo a prohibition, so the teaching seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב אשי: our cooked wine with a gentile needs only one seal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives the same kind of answer: the lesson is that a Jew's cooked wine left with gentiles needs only one seal, since gentiles don't pour cooked wine as an offering. His second reason continues on the next page.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This teaches that our cooked wine in gentiles' hands does not need a seal within a seal. If you worry about it being poured as an offering, they don't pour cooked wine. And if you worry about...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers just as he did for vinegar. A Jew's cooked wine left with gentiles needs only one seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooked wine is not used for idol offerings, so the first worry is gone. The second worry, swapping, is cut off at the end of this section. Following the vinegar case, we expect one seal to be enough for that too.

keyTerms.meaning: They pour (wine) as an idol offering

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This comes to teach us
that our cooked wine in the hands of gentiles
does not need a seal within a seal.
If because of pouring it as an offering, they don't pour it,
and if because of

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא אֲתָא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with the same reasoning רב אשי used for vinegar in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Hidden lesson: a related leniency about seals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seems only to say the obvious, that cooked wine stays forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cooked wine has a lighter status, so a Jew's cooked wine left with gentiles needs only one seal.
